steps_h2: How to Put Your Product in a Scene
steps_lead: The cream tote you already shot is enough to build the scene.

steps.d: Upload a photo where both straps and the base of the cream tote are visible.
Ask for a cafe table or a market stall. One nearby object, such as a cup, is enough to show use.
Check the straps against the white photo, then keep the square. Put the price on it yourself.

faq.q: What is a lifestyle photo of the product I sell?
faq.a: A lifestyle product photo shows the item in a place a buyer recognizes, made from the catalog photo you already have. A tote on a cafe table is one example. The bag stays the bag.

faq.q: How do I build a cafe scene from my tote photo?
faq.a: Use the catalog photo as the reference and name a place, such as a cafe table. Download the square when the straps still match the tote you uploaded.

faq.q: Can I publish the cafe scene on my product page?
faq.a: Yes. A tote shop can put the cafe-table square on the product page. Add the price yourself after you download the file.

faq.q: Can I pick a cafe, a shelf, or a market for my product?
faq.a: Yes. Name the kind of place, such as a cafe table, a room shelf, or a market stall. The product photo stays the reference. You can ask for a different place next.

faq.q: What can I still change after the tote scene is made?
faq.a: You can change the surface, or run a second scene from the same tote. Your store software can request one through the API.

faq.q: Can I try another place for the same tote?
faq.a: Yes. Start again with a different surface or one extra object. Each photo is 24 credits. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits. Pro is $35 for 300 credits, and Premium is $63 for 600.

faq.q: Does the cafe scene replace my plain tote photo?
faq.a: No. Keep the original for small details such as a stitch or a strap. Use the scene when you want shoppers to picture where the tote belongs.

faq.q: How is a staged tote photo different from a photoshoot?
faq.a: A shoot needs a place, a few extra objects, and a day on the calendar. Here you start from a photo you already have. If that photo is hard to read, start with [how to take product photos for AI](page:guide-product-photo-tips).

faq.q: Can I put the tote scene on my Shopify store?
faq.a: Yes. Download the square and upload it on the product page yourself.

faq.q: Can I post the tote scene on Instagram?
faq.a: Yes. The square works as the product photo in the feed. Write the caption in Instagram, and add any price in your own editor.

faq.q: Can I use the tote scene in a paid ad?
faq.a: Yes. Finish the headline and the offer in your ad editor. The photo does not include your price.

platforms.h2: Stage and Finish the Tote Photo
platforms.lead: Product staging starts here. Clean the catalog photo, stage the tote, size the file, and hand it to the person who posts it.

items.t: Change the Product Background
items.d: The tote can leave a cluttered counter and sit on a plain gray sweep.

items.t: Create a White or Brand-Color Background
items.d: Choose sand or a green that matches the label, and keep the tote color aligned to the uploaded photo.

items.t: Create a Lifestyle Product Scene
items.d: Put the tote on a cafe table, next to one cup and a folded napkin.

items.t: Fix Lighting, Clutter, and Image Size
items.d: A stray spoon beside the tote can go. Then fit the file to the slot the store asks for.

items.t: Put the Tote on an Actor
items.d: A tote can sit on a shoulder so the buyer sees the drop. That person is an AI actor.

items.t: Download a Store-Ready Square
items.d: Download the file and put it where you sell. The price is still something you add.

items.t: Improve Lighting and Color
items.d: If the white-background tote looks gray, even out the color before you build a scene on top of it.

items.t: Resize Photos for Each Placement
items.d: A story slot and a banner need different shapes. The tote photo can match each placement.

items.t: Request Product Scenes Through an API
items.d: Connect through the API and request a scene for a tote already on the list.

items.t: Add Text to Product Photos
items.d: The shop name can sit in a corner of the tote photo. Pricing stays in your ad editor.

items.t: Batch Edit Product Photos
items.d: Every tote in the catalog can get the same linen surface. You do not open a dozen files by hand.

items.t: Share Product Scenes With Your Team
items.d: Send the cafe scene to the person who owns the product page, before it goes live.

items.t: Save Logos, Fonts, and Brand Colors
items.d: Save the shop mark and the green you always use, so the next tote scene carries the same color.

items.t: Create a Simple Product Brand Mark
items.d: A new shop can make a simple mark here, then put that mark on the next scene.

items.t: Edit Product Photos Across Devices
items.d: Start the tote scene on a laptop and finish the crop on a phone.
